content.text:
Here are good **free online auto repair estimate** options:

1. **RepairPal Estimator** — best for common mechanical repairs like brakes, alternator, starter, water pump, AC, suspension, etc. It uses your ZIP code, vehicle info, parts, labor times, and local labor rates. Some RepairPal estimates may be guaranteed for 30 days at certified shops. ([repairpal.com](https://repairpal.com/estimator/repair-services?utm_source=openai))

2. **YourMechanic Instant Estimate** — good for mobile mechanic pricing and common maintenance/repair jobs. It gives a price breakdown for labor and parts and lets you book a mechanic who comes to you. ([yourmechanic.com](https://www.yourmechanic.com/estimates/?utm_source=openai))

3. **Otto / Vehicle Damage Calculator** — useful for **body damage**, dents, scratches, bumper damage, and collision estimates from photos. It gives an AI-based estimate quickly, but final body-shop pricing can vary after inspection. ([ottofixit.com](https://www.ottofixit.com/?utm_source=openai))

4. **VTCCO** — another free AI photo-based estimate tool for collision/body damage; it’s more geared toward accident cases and insurance/self-pay decisions. Its estimates are preliminary and should be confirmed by a licensed repair facility or adjuster. ([vtcco.com](https://vtcco.com/?utm_source=openai))

5. **RedAppy Estimate Generator** — if you’re a shop or DIY seller and need to **create a professional-looking estimate PDF**, not calculate market pricing, this tool lets you itemize labor, parts, vehicle details, taxes, and notes. ([redappy.com](https://www.redappy.com/tools/estimate-generator?utm_source=openai))

**Tip:** Online estimates are best as a ballpark. For an accurate quote, you’ll usually need your **year/make/model, engine size, mileage, ZIP code, symptoms or repair needed**, and sometimes photos or diagnostic codes.

If you tell me your **car year/make/model**, **ZIP code**, and what repair you need, I can help you estimate a reasonable price range.
